institutionName: University of Natural Resources and Life Sciences, Vienna (BOKU)

questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The courses and field of study I could follow at my host university

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Relatively easy. Even though there was quite a it of confusion the coordinators at the host university were very supportive and helpful.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer:
Orientation week
Introduction meetings
Emails with reminders and additional information

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: There were quite a lot of options for dorms but one had to be very quick and early to have a chance. Finding a shared flat or any other type of accommodation outside of a student dorm was relatively difficult.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Make sure to check the access of public transport in advance as BOKU is quite far from the city center so commuting to campus can take quite some time.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: A lot of the courses were already fully booked when I could start registering for courses (you first need to register at the university in person before you get access to the course registration). Some course registration started super early way before the mobility period and thus I had no chance of getting a place in several courses (BOKU does not have a course registration period, the registration period differs for each course and many courses only allow few people).

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Once you had an appointment at the study service it was super easy and quick to get registered.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer:
Study coordinator
International relations
Student organisations

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I did get some of the courses I wanted to take but sadly quite a few were discontinued or were already full by the time I was able to register for courses so that was a bit of a bummer (they also often overlap as there is no real structure with the course schedule).

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Do it as soon as possible as this will increase your chances to enrol in the courses you were interested in and figure out the schedule.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The courses were mostly introductory courses as BOKU has a unique system where most courses only have 1-3 ECTS so the course content is often rather superficial and can lack some depth depending on your own knowledge in that field. The number of ECTS does not tell you anything about the difficulty or workload of the course, it would be best to ask other students about the courses. My 1.5 ECTS course was the most intense with weekly lectures and assignments and a final 20 page manuscript ready to be submitted to a journal.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: A lot more passive learning (just listening to a lecturer and less interactive learning or group work), though there are also seminars that you can register for that have more group work and interactive aspects.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 2 semesters

Field Camp I - Introduction to mountain forestry and forest sciences
Scientific writing

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your second semester. *
questions.answer:
Research proposal
Master 's thesis 
Master's thesis seminar

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Human impacts in riverine landscapes 
Ecological river landscape management 
Field Camp I - Introduction to mountain forestry and forest sciences
Air pollution effects on forest ecosystems 
Soil ecology 

These courses were all super fun to take and I also learned a lot and feel like I will be able to use that knowledge in the future.

questions.answer:
some courses require you to pay a fee (e.g. excursions)

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: the prices did not differ so much between Copenhagen and Vienna but groceries might be a bit cheaper in Austria.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
BOKU ball
Sport courses from the sport institute 
lots of social activities such as crafting days, live music and so on and also international student organisations organising trips and fun activities

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
BOKU ball -> was such a unique and great experience to wear either a nice ball dress or traditional Austrian dress and then spend the night in the downhill which looks like something out of a fairy tale.

ESN student organisation --> lots of cool city trips and fun activities to connect and meet new people (I met most of my friends there).

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
city trips to experience other cities in Austria but also the neighbouring cities (Brno, Bratislava)
Skiing in winter 
Hiking
Swimming in the Danube in summer 
going to Heuriger and walking through the vineyards 
going to the theatre or opera

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: relatively easy as I have been in Austria many times before but it is a bit different from Copenhagen

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: people are often very direct and have a dry sense of humour which might be a bit startling at first

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer:
the film festival in August- October which is for free and you can watch many great operas
I also really enjoyed the many concerts, operas and museums you can go to

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
don't be too shocked by the amount of courses (around 10-14) you will have to take at the same time.
Try to go to the introduction week as you will learn many helpful things and potentially meet your new friends
Try to take a few courses where you don't have to pass an exam as 14 exams in a month is quite a lot. 
There is no exam period, exams can be written at any point during the semester but often you will have several dates you can choose from

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be ready to have cash on you as not everything can be paid by card

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The people I have met and the cultural activities such as the operas and concerts I have been to as well as all the traditional food I ate

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Managing the course schedule and trying to minimise the overlap.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
